findings.title: Public group members list is capped at 50 with no pagination
findings.body: The public group members route now calls Group.findMembers(), which always requests limit 50 (Discourse.Group default, and GroupsController#members defaults to 50 and always applies limit/offset). The members template only renders that page and has no next/previous or load-more control, unlike the new admin UI. Non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups previously returned up to 200. Groups larger than 50 now look complete while everyone after the first page is omitted, with no indication of the total.

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when the member count is a multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. That is correct only when the count is not divisible by the page size. For 50 members and limit 50 it yields 2 instead of 1; for 100 it yields 3 instead of 2. showingLast stays false on the real last page, so Next stays enabled. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers loads an empty page, and the UI shows a phantom last page (for example 2/2 or 3/3 with no members). Use ceil(user_count / limit), and do not treat offset == user_count as a valid page.

findings.title: Creating a group drops the selected alias level
findings.body: The new-group form shows the alias-level combo (it is outside the {{#if id}} block) and Group.asJSON posts alias_level, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible before save. alias_level stays at the database default (0 / nobody) no matter what the admin picked. The client only copies basic_group.id from the response, so the form still shows the unsaved choice until a full reload. A second Save happens to persist it via update, but leaving the page or refreshing loses the setting. Update already honors alias_level; create does not, and the create spec only checks name stripping.

findings.title: Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page
findings.body: removeMember reloads via findMembers() without moving offset backward. findMembers clamps offset with the pre-delete user_count (Math.min(user_count, offset)), so an offset already on the last page is kept. The server echoes that offset even when it is past the new end (GroupsController#members does not clamp). Example: 51 members, limit 50, page 2 shows one user; after that user is removed the request still uses offset 50, the response is an empty list with total 50, and the admin stays on an empty page until they click Previous.

findings.title: Group update treats a missing visible flag as false and ignores the old payload
findings.body: update always does group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" and reads name/alias_level from top-level params. The previous API (and any cached admin JS, plugin, or script) sent a nested group hash and could PATCH incremental membership changes. Those requests no longer include top-level visible, so this saves visible=false and returns 200, hiding the group, while name, alias_level, and usernames in group[...] are ignored and PATCH add/remove is gone. A missing or old-format update therefore persists a visibility change the caller did not make. Reject the old shape or read both params[:visible] and params[:group], and do not default visibility to false when the key is absent.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members JSON shape changed from an array to an object
findings.body: members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects, which the old client mapped directly. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}} and always paginates (default 50). The in-repo Group model was updated, but any other client, plugin, or cached script that still expects a JSON array will throw when it calls .map (or will only see the first page if it adapts). This is an unversioned break of a public group endpoint; old and new payloads are not accepted together.

findings.title: Add and remove member failures are silent, and the add field is never cleared
findings.body: addMembers() ignores the promise from model.addMembers(), and removeMember() ignores removeMember()'s promise. There is no error callback, so a 422, 500, or network failure closes the dialog or clicks Add and leaves the list unchanged with no alert. On success the username field is not cleared (the TODO on the previous line), and findMembers() only reloads the current offset, so a new user who sorts onto another page never appears. The server also returns 200 when every username is unknown (add_members skips failed lookups and still saves), so a typo is indistinguishable from success. Admins cannot tell whether membership changed.

findings.title: Member page changes race and can display the wrong page
findings.body: next and previous update group.offset and call findMembers() with no in-flight guard, and the links stay clickable until the response updates showingFirst/showingLast. Two quick clicks issue overlapping requests. findMembers() writes members, user_count, and offset from whichever response settles last, not from the latest offset. A slower request for an earlier page can overwrite a later one, so the pager and the member list disagree until another navigation. The same pattern applies to previous().

findings.title: Update does not strip group names, and create does not sync the stripped name back
findings.body: create saves (params[:name] || '').strip, but the client only applies resp.basic_group.id and keeps the raw name (including leading/trailing spaces). update then does group.name = params[:name] with no strip. The admin list therefore shows the unstripped name after create. The next Save posts that raw name; the placeholder says names cannot contain spaces, so validation fails and the rest of the edit is discarded, or a spaced name is stored even though create had already normalized it. Apply the serialized name after create and strip on update the same way as create.

findings.title: New members pagination and admin member routes are untested at the HTTP layer
findings.body: GroupsController#members changed from a full (or 200-row) array to a paginated {members, meta} object, and there is no spec for the default limit, offset, total, or response shape, so the public 50-member truncation would not fail CI. Admin add_members/remove_member specs call the actions directly with group_id and never go through config/routes.rb. A member route that supplies :id instead of :group_id, or a path that does not match /admin/groups/:id/members, would 400/404 in the browser while these specs stay green. The automatic remove example even uses xhr :put against an action routed as DELETE.
